inScope: Initial public registration of adoption interest for an animal.
A reviewable proposal for later staff handling of registered interest.
A proposed use of the AVAILABLE status when accepting interest.
outOfScope: Applicant screening, authentication, automatic approval, and the complete adoption process.
An implemented staff-review interface or API.
Returning applicant data from public animal-profile responses.

assumptions: Consent wording, applicant-data retention, duplicate-interest handling, and privacy review require validation before implementation.
Later staff handling requires a protected operational capability, but its interface and access model are not defined in the supplied evidence.
An adoption-interest record may need applicant contact data; the exact fields are not defined in the supplied evidence.

alternatives.description: Keep the current public profile link as a future placeholder and defer initial interest registration until the broader adoption prototype.
alternatives.consequence: Avoids introducing applicant data before unresolved privacy and policy questions are validated, but does not address the evolution concern in the current increment.

alternatives.description: Add a bounded adoption-interest capability: a public animal-profile form submits initial interest to a dedicated application/API boundary, which persists an Animal-related AdoptionInterest concept for later staff handling.
alternatives.consequence: Addresses initial interest without implementing screening or approval. Applicant data must remain outside public animal-profile responses, and consent, retention, duplicates, and privacy controls remain validation work.

alternatives.description: Extend the existing Animal update or status-update endpoints to store initial interest directly on Animal.
alternatives.consequence: May appear smaller, but mixes a future planned AdoptionInterest concern into Animal and creates unclear applicant-data visibility and status semantics. It is not preferred without additional domain and privacy validation.

selectedOption.rationale: A dedicated, bounded interest capability aligns with the planned AdoptionInterest concept while preserving the separation of interface, application, domain, and infrastructure responsibilities. It delivers only initial registration and leaves screening, authentication, approval, and staff operations for later increments.

webContext.interactionFlow: A visitor opens a public animal profile, uses the existing interest entry point, submits an initial-interest form, and receives a submission outcome. The submitted record is retained for later staff handling; no staff-review workflow is implemented in this increment.
boundaries: The public animal profile currently exposes animal data and contains an interest link, but no interest form is implemented.
The current Animals API has no adoption-interest endpoint.
Applicant data must not be included in public animal-profile responses.
A dedicated application/API capability is proposed for initial-interest submission; its exact DTO and persistence design require implementation design work.
webContext.dataVisibility: Public animal-profile responses remain limited to public Animal data. Any applicant data introduced for initial interest is excluded from those responses and is reserved for later staff handling.
qualityAttributes: Privacy: applicant data requires validation of consent, retention, and exposure boundaries.
Traceability: the proposal should preserve an Animal-related interest record for later staff handling.
Incremental delivery: the capability is limited to initial registration and excludes the complete adoption process.

domainRules.rule: Initial interest acceptance is proposed only for an Animal with status AVAILABLE. AVAILABLE is an existing status value; whether recording interest changes status requires an explicit future transition policy and is not a current rule.
The increment records initial interest only and must not implement screening, authentication, automatic approval, or a complete adoption process.
Applicant data, if introduced, must not be returned by public animal-profile responses.
Consent, retention, duplicate-interest handling, and privacy controls are unresolved and require validation before they become domain or application rules.

validation: Define the minimum applicant-data fields and confirm whether their collection is necessary for later staff handling.
Validate consent text, retention duration, deletion expectations, and privacy controls for applicant data.
Define duplicate-interest policy, including whether repeated interest for the same animal is allowed and how it is identified.
Decide whether accepted initial interest leaves Animal as AVAILABLE or triggers a future explicit transition policy.
Define the later staff-handling boundary, including access control and review workflow, without implementing it in this increment.
Confirm API contracts ensure public animal-profile responses never include applicant data.
documentationUpdates: Create a versioned ADR documenting the bounded initial-interest capability, public/private data boundary, use of AVAILABLE, and deferred transition-policy decision.
Update the architecture documentation to describe the proposed adoption-interest application, domain, and infrastructure boundaries.
Update the functional scope documentation to include initial interest registration and explicitly retain screening, authentication, and complete adoption as out of scope.
Update the domain diagram to show Animal-related AdoptionInterest as an incrementally introduced concept and mark later staff handling as deferred.
Add or update a reusable prompt for reviewing adoption-interest privacy, retention, duplicate policy, and status-transition assumptions.
